portion_doctrine: AI-powered B2B local agency arbitrage. High-ticket law/med/fitness/data-center clients. Front-end human trust, back-end 90% AI. Off-camera operator model. Revenue via corporate sessions ($1,500 team, ~94% margin), authority book ($29-47), photographer community validation loop. 30-day execution plan with locked operating rules (no em-dashes/buzzwords, 95/5 content split, 20% cultural hijack, trim-glitches, 2-3 clients/month at $800-$1,500 baseline).
operating_rules: No em-dashes in any copy—AI-detection signal
No buzzwords: amazing, stunning, hustle, journey, grind
80/20 Rule: 80% core expertise, 20% experimental off-speed pitches
Upscale Rule (Kling): always upscale stills before animating to preserve fidelity
Anti-Glitch Rule: trim final 10 frames of Kling clips to avoid morphing, hard cuts on audio beat
Cultural Hijack (20% Rule): 20% content is reactive/trend-based, NOT consumer holidays
RAW File Rule: never deliver RAW files, they are unfinished ingredients
Visual Directive Gate: require visual directive before booking confirmation
Maybe Filter: does this make viewer stop scrolling? If no, kill it
Rejection-as-Moat: side hustle framing becomes competitive advantage
Pacing Rule: never run identical hooks across platforms
2-Hour SLA: respond to inquiries within 2 hours (trigger metric if missed twice)
Perception is Infrastructure: rebuilding it changes everything
Tone: calm authority, real but elevated. NOT 'Perception Engineer'
Casualness over polish: casual copy outperforms polished marketing copy

contradictions_and_tensions: Gumroad book is $0 revenue but massive positioning cost: it trains buyers to trust before $1,500 ask (funnel paradox)
90% AI production but off-camera operator = invisibility paradox; authority comes via 3rd-party photographer testimonials, not direct credibility
Casual copy outperforms polished copy, but entire model is built on 'calm authority, elevated' tone (grittiness beats perfection)
Side-hustle framing becomes moat (rejection advantage), yet requiring $1,500+ session price points (premium positioning paradox)
weird_gold: Perception is Infrastructure: 'Bad photo' is read as 'company ignores details'—rebuilding perception changes entire revenue model
Trim Last 10 Frames = Invisible AI: Kling always breaks at the end; hard rule reveals photorealism only
The Maybe Filter: content evaluation gate (does this make you stop scrolling?) applies to copy/positioning/hooks equally
Rejection as Moat: 'I do this on the side' turns scrappiness into trust signal vs. full-time agency
Photographer Loop: 5 photographers are NOT clients; they're social proof salesmen who validate your system to business owners
Month 1 Reality Check: $10K/month is fake guru logic; realistic baseline is 6-8 sessions + book (breaking the scaling myth)
The Operator Doctrine Echo: revenue flows through OTHERS (photographers, law firm partners) so founder stays off-camera and scalable
